title: A source-plus-index type with no parser attached
body:
nail is to use libsail to frame and index its sequence and profile databases while parsing each record's bytes into its own types. Reader<R> already hands out raw bytes, and Index, Source and Parse are public, but the pair of a Source and an Index exists only inside IndexedFasta, IndexedStockholm and IndexedHmm, each of which carries its own copy and is reachable only through a type named for a parser. The three copies differ in which parser try_get calls and which name_of name_index calls, and in nothing else.

## Decision

Give the source-plus-index pair its own concrete type, and have the three format collections wrap it instead of each carrying a copy. nail wraps the same type with its own parser, so it is not a special case: libsail's own formats are the worked example.

- A struct in index.rs beside Reader, holding `source: S` and `index: Index`, generic over Source as the Indexed* types already are and over nothing else. Working name `Framed<S>`; the name is open.
- Constructors mirror Reader: `open(path, format)` scans, `detect(path)` sniffs the first bytes, `with_index(path, index)` takes the format from the index, and `unsafe map(path, format)` on the MmapSource impl.
- Methods: `format()`, `index()`, `len()`, `name_index()` dispatching on the index's format through seq::name_of, and `record(n) -> Result<Option<Cow<[u8]>>>`. All exist today on each Indexed* type; none is new.
- IndexedFasta<S> becomes a newtype over Framed<S> that keeps its current constructors, forwards index, name_index and record, and adds try_get, validate and Indexable. Its with_index keeps the format check, since this is the type that promises FASTA. Stockholm and Hmm likewise. sail's call sites and output bytes do not move.
- nail: `struct Fasta(Framed<MmapSource>)` built with `Framed::map(db, Format::Fasta)`, name lookup through index().position, get through record(n) and its own parse. Profiles the same over Format::Hmm. Streaming stays on Reader.

## Rejected

1. `Indexed<P: Parse, S: Source>` with the three types as aliases. It collapses the same copies, but P has three instantiations inside libsail, below the threshold for a type parameter, and no generic consumer: Indexable is what the combinators bind, and each wrapper implements it directly. The aliases needed their own impl blocks for the old one-argument constructors anyway, and name_index dispatched on the runtime Format regardless, so P bought try_get and nothing else, at the cost of a parameter and a PhantomData in every signature nail sees.
2. Framing as a type parameter, `Indexed<P, D: Delimit, S>`, with Index dropping its Format field. Proposed from the nail side for a consumer-supplied delimiter, which by its own account nothing in nail uses. The .saidx header persists the format byte, so Index::write would have to take the format as a parameter, which the api rule forbids, and with_index's check of a foreign .saidx against the collection would go.
3. libsail owning nail's Sequence and Profile. Those encodings belong to nail's DP kernels. libsail knows where a record is; nail knows what it means.

## Out of scope

A consumer-supplied Delimit, and a database whose offsets come from a separate file rather than a scan: sail-f85dea. Under this design that is a constructor on the concrete type rather than a new parser.

## Versioning

libsail minor bump: the three Indexed* types change from structs with fields to newtypes, and a new public type appears. sail's command line and output do not move, and tests/cli.rs is what says so.

## Open

1. The name of the concrete type.
2. Index::build walks a Reader where IndexedFasta::open today calls build_index::<_, FastaDelimiter>, the chunked scan. Same offsets either way; whether they cost the same is a benchmark question, and a format-keyed build_index is a short dispatcher if not.
close_reason: Framed<S> landed on dev with the three collections as newtypes over it; see the commit after dcaecb1

notes.author: Jack Roddy/c45d6630
notes.text: Jack approved the concrete design on 2026-10-09 after the generic Indexed<P, S> shape was costed against the concrete-first counting rules and rejected. Not yet claimed; implementation waits on his go.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/c45d6630
notes.text: Built as Framed<S> in index.rs, with a private format-keyed build_for beside delim_of so open(path, format) takes the same chunked scan the collections took before; Index::build through Reader was left alone, so the open point about their relative cost is moot for this change. The three collections are newtypes with every public signature kept. Not a breaking change after all: the fields were private, so nothing outside the crate could see the struct become a tuple. Six tests cover Framed against Reader, detect, with_index, build_named, IndexedFasta and the map.
